bullets.title: NVDA: 15%+ AI price hikes, earnings week catalyst, Perplexity deal & Vera Rubin ramp
bullets.body: Nvidia is raising AI server prices 15%+ driven by memory cost surge, with customers including Microsoft notified in advance. MSFT CEO Nadella confirmed first production Vera Rubin deliveries at Microsoft DCs. Simultaneously, Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest billions (~$6B deal + broader Perplexity investment) to distribute open-weight models and compete with DeepSeek—framed as strategic model distribution rather than charity. NVDA also extended its 6-day losing streak (longest in 4 years), and Broadcom CDS hit record 122 while NVDA CDS hit all-time wides post-earnings week.

bullets.title: HBM/Memory: Samsung zHBM 70% power cut, custom HBM competition, Micron $10B AI R&D
bullets.body: Hot Chips featured major memory innovation: Samsung roadmapped zHBM targeting 70% power reduction vs HBM5; all accelerator companies are pursuing 3D DRAM or zHBM variants. SK Hynix published CPO roadmap in Nature Electronics. Micron CEO said 'no end' to when supply catches up with demand, and MU announced $10B dedicated AI memory R&D center timed strategically ahead of SK Hynix's Indiana groundbreaking. NAND tungsten-to-molybdenum conversion creates >$1B equipment opportunity in 2027.

bullets.title: TSM: Record $40.2B revenue, 67.7% gross margin, $265B Arizona commitment
bullets.body: TSMC posted all-time revenue and margin highs in 2Q26 with operating margin exceeding 60% for the first time. Arizona commitment reached $265B with Phase 1 already profitable; an additional $100B is going toward four more fabs on 2nm-and-below logic. N3 remains the supply bottleneck of the AI cycle with three new fabs under construction. Separately, TSMC is rumored to spend ~$940M acquiring AUO display plants for advanced packaging conversion (CoPoS/FOPLP), and partnering with Largan Precision on CPO for AI applications.

bullets.title: INTC: Foundry inflects—external revenue +68% q/q, OCI strong in CPO/ASIC
bullets.body: Intel Foundry operating loss narrowed $348M q/q with external revenue surging 68% to $293M on yield and cycle-time improvements across Intel 4/3/18A. Intel's optics process and EMIB technology could unlock co-packaged optics advantage; Intel expects more design wins with MSFT and MRVL in ASIC, CPU, and CPO. Two Intel CPUs re-entered Amazon's top 10 best-selling list after >1 year absence.

bullets.title: BABA: $10.2B HK share placement for AI investment triggers 8-10% selloff
bullets.body: Alibaba launched its largest-ever primary follow-on offering—710M shares at HK$112.70, a 3.6% discount—to fund full-stack AI capabilities. Hong Kong shares fell 8-10% at open on dilution concerns. Michael Burry criticized the deal as AI spending cuts profits 75%.

bullets.title: META: $1T+ California antitrust trial creates near-term underperformance overhang
bullets.body: A $1.4 trillion trial brought by a multi-state AG coalition opened in Oakland under Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers (the Epic v. Apple judge). Trial focuses on civil penalties and market distortion over six to seven weeks. Multiple accounts see META underperforming the S&P near-term as the litigation overhang mounts—compared to tobacco cases of 30 years ago.

bullets.title: AAOI: Repeated ATM dilution ($500-600M) undermines sentiment despite optical growth
bullets.body: Applied Optonics filed for a possible share offering via Raymond James and Needham post-market, sending shares -2.3%. Author notes back-to-back ATM offerings totaling $500-600M are making the stock hard to support despite a positive operating backdrop; management had telegraphed equity financing on the earnings call. Rosenblatt laid out strategies to reduce future reliance on ATMs but timing is uncertain.

bullets.title: AAPL: Cuts 200+ jobs in Siri, Vision Pro, 3D video, and gaming teams; CXMT memory rumor
bullets.body: Apple is cutting over 200 jobs across Siri, Vision Pro, 3D video, and gaming teams per Bloomberg. Separately, Trump is reportedly set to allow Apple to source memory chips from Chinese maker CXMT for China-market iPhones after a planned Trump-Xi September meeting; Apple faces DRAM supply constraints that aren't price-driven.

bullets.title: TSLA: FSD Cybercab event Sept 3, China recall 4.3M vehicles, 4680 cathode ramp
bullets.body: Tesla posted a Cybercab/full self-driving event for September 3. China ordered a recall of 4.3M vehicles from Tesla and 8 other automakers over a door defect. On the positive side, Tesla is operating the first large-scale cathode production facility in North America in Austin for 4680 cells. JPMorgan toured Fremont factory as humanoid production nears. Elon claims Optimus will be 'vastly superior' to anything China can make.

bullets.title: Silicon wafer prices rising 10% first time in 3+ years on AI demand
bullets.body: Silicon wafer prices set to rise 10%—the first major hike in over 3 years—across all wafer sizes (6", 8", 12"), as AI-driven demand has absorbed excess supply. GPU/VRAM supply constraints also driving graphics card makers to consider further price hikes on Nvidia RTX 5050/3060 series.

bullets.title: SMCI: Board probe clears senior management in alleged $2.5B China smuggling scheme
bullets.body: Super Micro's board-led independent investigation found no evidence current senior management knew about an alleged $2.5B hardware smuggling scheme involving Nvidia chips destined for China. Taiwan prosecutors separately named Nvidia and Supermicro employees as defendants in an undisclosed case.

bullets.title: US-Canada trade war escalates: 50% tariffs in effect, Canada retaliates Sept 8
bullets.body: US-Canada trade talks collapsed late Friday night; the US imposed 50% Section 338 tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods (alcohol, hockey equipment, etc.). Canada's PM Carney suspended negotiations, pledging dollar-for-dollar retaliation effective September 8, targeting steel, dairy, and electronics. USTR Greer said no new talks are planned. Canada's CAD strengthened amid broader USD weakness.

bullets.title: Macro: Bond yields surge, gold at 3-month highs, Treasury buybacks as quasi-QE
bullets.body: 30-year Treasury yields hit 5.27%, the highest weekly close since June 2007. Gold surged to $4,700 (3-month high) and near $4,650 spot on flight-to-safety and Bessent's quasi-QE Treasury buyback program. Treasury debt held by public surpassed 100% of GDP. Japan sold $26B in Treasuries in June alone ($123B since February), reducing holdings to January 2025 lows. BofA fund manager cash at 3.5%—6th-lowest since 1998—signals contrarian sell.

bullets.title: JPMorgan flags growing late-summer/early-fall market downturn risk
bullets.body: JPMorgan strategist Jason Hunter flagged growing risks of a market downturn in late summer or early autumn despite major indices remaining in bullish trends. SPY closing in bottom half of its intraday range almost every day for two weeks—unprecedented near recent highs—signals unusual trader anxiety about overnight risk. Chip/memory trade peak correlated with total return swap funding costs hitting record highs in June.

bullets.title: UBER: €825M GDPR fine from Dutch authorities for automated driver suspensions
bullets.body: Dutch regulators fined Uber €825M ($963M)—the second-largest GDPR penalty on record—for using automated systems to suspend driver accounts improperly. Separately, Manhattan service reliability has deteriorated dramatically with ~50% driver no-shows at elevated prices.

bullets.title: MRVL: $12.2B Google TPU deal and Jensen's $1T valuation call drive focus
bullets.body: Marvell's two recent catalysts—a $12.2B Google TPU ecosystem agreement and Jensen Huang's suggestion that MRVL could become a $1T company—are driving market attention. Post-earnings supply chain checks maintain a positive view alongside INTC. NVDA's CoWoS share at TSM expected stable in 2027.

bullets.title: AMZN: Autonomous vehicles deploying in SF/Las Vegas; Echo/Kindle price hikes on memory costs
bullets.body: Amazon's fully autonomous vehicles (no steering wheel, no pedals) are active in San Francisco streets and charging for rides in Las Vegas with up to 4 passengers. Amazon separately raised prices on Echo, Fire TV, Kindle, and eero products citing 'significant increases' in memory costs—the same dynamic affecting Nvidia's server pricing.

bullets.title: PLTR: Trump disclosed June purchase; Pentagon allocated $244M post-trade; stock +58%
bullets.body: President Trump filed a June 24 purchase of Palantir stock. The Pentagon directed up to $244M for Palantir in a memo dated August 4. PLTR has risen 58% since Trump's trade, raising conflict-of-interest questions that the White House says are moot as the accounts use computer-based model portfolios replicating indexes.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk: Iran Hormuz threat, oil near $85-94, tanker traffic collapse
bullets.body: Iran threatened to halt all oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz if neighbors join US economic pressure; vessel traffic collapsed to a single ship per day at peak tension, with 80%+ of transits routing via Oman's alternative passage. Brent settled at $94.39. US crude slid 2% to $85.23 at one point as Bessent announced an 'economic D-Day' against Iran's financial system for Monday. US SPR fell to lowest since December 1982 (41 days of supply). LME copper orders surged 51,400 tons (most since May).

bullets.title: Foundry industry record; Taiwan OSAT $14.4B capex; data center opposition rising
bullets.body: The global foundry industry hit a record $54.5B in 2Q26, up 28% YoY with supply only +6%, meaning growth is pricing- and mix-driven. Taiwan's Big 5 OSATs plan $14.4B capex this year driven by AI demand. Data center opposition intensifying: 71% of Gallup respondents oppose local data center construction vs. 53% for nuclear plants. Trump warned communities rejecting data centers are 'making mistakes.'
